name: Tantalus-Veil
description: Under the doubled light of its binary suns, Tantalus-Veil hangs like a coin of beaten gold, cloud bands streaked amber and cream and shadowed by a ring of debris bright as spilled sugar. A single storm—the Veil—wraps the entire equator in a slow white ribbon visible from neighboring systems. Sunrises here come twice, and both set the ring burning.

Nothing lands; nothing survives landing. The dense atmosphere strips sensor returns at two hundred kilometers and dissolves probe hulls long before any instrument reaches solid reference. What the giant offers instead is blindness: radar-eating haze decks, gravity gradients that scatter pursuit solutions, ring shadows deep enough to lose a fleet in.

Which is how the Tatterwake corsairs have held it for thirty years. Their dock—a captured liner gutted and re-rigged—drifts somewhere in the upper haze bands, striking helium convoys and vanishing into the Veil's storm ribbon. Rumor adds a pre-Imperial smuggler cache among the inner moonlets: antimatter containment bottles from a war no treaty mentions, still cold, still full.

Three navies have mounted suppression operations into those clouds; none returned with prisoners, wreckage, or explanations. The bounty on Tatterwake's leadership now exceeds most planets' defense budgets, and every free-trader in the sector can recite the dock's rumored coordinates—which is precisely why no one says them aloud.
